subject.title: Feature request: add prefix/list-style skill discovery to ClawHub CLI search

question: Should ClawHub make deterministic exact/prefix registry discovery a supported public CLI/API mode, and if so, what completeness, ordering, cap, and pagination guarantees should that contract provide?
rationale: Current code deliberately combines literal recall with relevance ranking, while the requested behavior turns that surface into a public enumeration contract. The open PR supplies a plausible implementation, but it cannot establish the long-term API semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded exact/prefix modes
options.body: Adopt explicit exact and prefix search modes with documented deterministic ordering, a defined cap, and pagination behavior, then review the linked PR against that contract.

options.title: Keep search relevance-only
options.body: Retain ranked search and direct users to existing browse/explore workflows rather than promising namespace enumeration through search.

options.title: Design a broader registry listing API
options.body: Defer the PR while specifying a separate list/filter API if publisher, namespace, and complete-catalog filtering are required together.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact/prefix modes
recommendation.body: Adopt explicit exact and prefix search modes with documented deterministic ordering, a defined cap, and pagination behavior, then review the linked PR against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is principally about ClawHub’s public discovery-product boundary described in the repository vision.
